title: Headless Squire's Bogey Pie
tagline: A harvest supper pudding that wobbles back at you.

ingredients.item: spare ghostly pumpkin head, lost at a crossroads
troll toenail clippings, crushed to a crust

steps:
Carve the pumpkin head with a grin,
then tip the bogey custard in.

Crush troll toenails, crunchy and grey,
and press them down for a crust this way.

Wring the sock till the sludge runs free,
then stir widdershins, thirteen times three.

Sprinkle the scales, then cobweb floss,
and drizzle the moon on top, gloss by gloss.

Set it by the gate till the midnight bell,
then serve a squire who's lost his head as well.
rhyme:
Round the cauldron, stamp and hum,
In plops a pumpkin head, hollow and glum.
Three green ladles of goblin snot,
Stirred till it wobbles, a gloopy lot.
Thirteen toenails from a troll's big feet,
Crunch them up for a crusty treat.
Swamp sludge next, and my old grey sock,
Wrung out slowly round the clock.
A sprinkle of scales, a web of fluff,
Moon-drizzle over: that's quite enough!
image_prompt: A lopsided dark pie in a rustic tin, its crust made of grey crunchy troll toenail shards, oozing bright green bogey custard over the edge. A hollow carved pumpkin head sits on top, grinning, draped with pale cobweb candyfloss, shimmering dragon scales and a limp grey sock hanging off the side.
alt_text: A wonky pie with a toenail crust, green slime oozing out, topped with a grinning pumpkin head, cobweb floss, shiny scales and a grey sock.
caption_hook:
Tonight's pudding comes with a toenail crust and a sock on top. A nod to the old Sleepy Hollow harvest supper, if the supper fought back.
Would you take the first slice, or send the headless squire in first?
